title: There Will Be Blood - Daniel and Eli as critique of Capitalist virtues

commenti.body:
Great write up.

One thing I always wondered was if Eli was happy in his interpersonal life aside from money. If he was emotionally fulfilled by the praise of his church or family. 

If Daniel is the quintessential portrait of capitalism and the church isn’t the way to salvation either, what does the film think is? If Daniel was an amazing father or brother would he have been anywhere near as successful? Would I? I don’t think the film is nihilistic but I can assume that it’s hard to find the correct moral answer besides a healthy work/life balance lol

>Great write up.

Hey, thanks.

>One thing I always wondered was if Eli was happy in his interpersonal life aside from money. If he was emotionally fulfilled by the praise of his church or family. 

Yeah, it's hard to get a grip on that side of Eli. Maybe he does have some kind of relationship with his family/the townsfolk, or maybe he really doesn't care about having relationships, and in that way is more inhuman than Daniel, who was at least tormented by his lack thereof.

>If Daniel is the quintessential portrait of capitalism and the church isn’t the way to salvation either, what does the film think is? If Daniel was an amazing father or brother would he have been anywhere near as successful? Would I? I don’t think the film is nihilistic but I can assume that it’s hard to find the correct moral answer besides a healthy work/life balance lol

I would think it would be H.W. making the best of his life even after losing his hearing and marrying someone he loves. He's the only person in the film who managed to put down Daniel.

Daniel didn't lose his brother, he killed him.  Also, Daniel doesn't embody the typical capitalist virtues of his time, he far exceeds them.  There were several scenes in the movie that contrasted him to the oilmen of his time.  "If you ever need a lawyer, son" and "don't tell me how to run my family" come to mind.

In my opinion, we don't know exactly what happened to Daniel, what caused him to be this way.  But I think that he is more than a symbol for capitalism.  There is something more to his character; it's almost like he's cursed.  He is right about Eli, isn't he?  He is right about his brother, isn't he?  Is this curse self-inflicted, a result of his totally un-Christian behavior?  Here is a man who has faked an entire relationship with HW and he won't even bless the well.  And was that why HW was injured?  On that level, I find the movie mesmerizing.  A battle over meaning.

Oh, I agree he's not just a symbol for capitalism, it's just part of him. Daniel is weirdly uncomfortable with other people. I think "I dn't want others to succeed, I hate most people" speech is rooted in some general discomfort with human relationships. But he still needs relationships like a normal person does. I think that's his curse. He shouldn't have keps the false brother around, but he should have had someone else to be open with. I think there's something in Daniel having such difficulty having relationships contrasted with Eli being a religious leader, but I can't work out what.

As for Eli, he's a charlatan, but Daniel was refusing to pay him his fair share for his land. It's a thing often forgotten in the slapping scene that Eli dous have a point tha Daniel ows him that money.

I do think he has some real love for H.W., he wouldn't have kept him around after he stopped being useful otherwise.

Really great post.  My perspective on the movie is that it is partially a commentary on the dominant institutions in society switching from religious to corporate ones.  What's important here is that both Eli and Daniel are, fundamentally, trying to trick the townspeople.  We see that Eli has been successful in this regard already, but Daniel is able to outmaneuver him, partially due to strength like you say, but also due to superior resources.  I think it comments the issues with religion controlling society, as well as how the secular institutions that usurped its place echo that same corruption and rot but at a higher and more industrialized scale.

Thank you for the write up. Maybe you are one i can ask. There is one thing about the movie that has always mystified me. Daniel has quickly dispatched/killed me who have gotten in his way. jungle laws seem to apply. Why didnt he just kill eli and take everything? Thank you.
His “brother” was a drifter with no connections to anyone in town. No one would care or come looking. Eli had family and friends. It wouldn’t have been easy or clean.

That's a very interesting way to look at their fight, thanks. You could probably say the film explores the power dynamics of religion vs buisness through Eli's need for Daniel's money and Daniel's lack of need for and contempt for Eli's religion.
I think Daniel is less "cursed" than he is an elemental force or the devil
Okay, thanks. I guess i over estimated daniel machialivan behavior. He never seemed to care what other people though. Maybe thats just ddl internal performance
